june-acme: Hi team — our streaming responses from the Dedicated instance in prod cut off mid-payload about half the time. Client sees partial JSON then connection closes. Reconnect resumes but the next stream contains duplicated tokens and we got billed for both. Repro steps below.

june-acme: Repro (curl):
```
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4r","prompt":"long output"}' \
  https://dedicated.us-west.redwood/api/stream
```

june-acme: behavior: stream starts, ~3-10s in we see truncated SSE chunk then client shows "connection reset". Reconnect with same session token -> server resumes but previous partial tokens are replayed and billing records show both segments billed.

sophia-support: thanks @june-acme — can you confirm Dedicated (not Private on-prem)? which VPC region and do you have a corporate proxy/ingress in front of the VPC? any MTU customizations? :thinking_face:

june-acme: Dedicated in us-west (AZ b). Yes, traffic passes through our corp proxy appliance (HTTP(S) inspect) then NAT into the VPC. MTU on their appliance is 1500, our ENIs are set to 9000 for jumbo frames.

matt-eng-runtime: interesting — jumbo frames on backend + 1500 MTU at proxy can cause IP fragmentation on the path. SSE is sensitive because we stream small chunked events; if an intermediate device collapses or reassembles fragments poorly you can get truncated TCP payloads. any TCP reset logs? also paste app/server logs if possible.

june-acme: we dug up tcpdump from the ingress:
```
15:02:03.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.443 > 10.1.1.22.56789: Flags [.], seq 1234567:1235123, ack 987654, win 65535, length 556
15:02:03.123789 IP 10.0.5.12.443 > 10.1.1.22.56789: Flags [R], seq 1235123, ack 987654, win 0, length 0
```
We also see DF set sometimes and fragmented packets other times.

eli-netops: that aligns with MSS/MSS-clamp issues + proxy doing TLS inspect + re-chunking. Some proxies convert chunked transfer into buffered responses which kills streaming semantics; others reassemble then prematurely close idle connections. Which proxy vendor?

june-acme: vendor is NetShield XG (corporate). They do TLS inspect and have an HTTP/1.0 translator option.

matt-eng-runtime: two likely failure modes here: 1) proxy disables Transfer-Encoding: chunked or buffers responses until full payload -> client sees partial then connection closed, 2) MTU fragmentation / reassembly bug causing mid-TCP-payload drop and server treats as RST. Both can lead to duplicate billing when client reconnects and server doesn't know the previous incomplete bytes were already consumed or client replays tokens.

sophia-support: quick mitigation options we can suggest to customer while engineering investigates:
- switch to non-streaming endpoint (polling) temporarily to avoid SSE billing duplicates
- have proxy enable true streaming passthrough / disable response buffering for the Redwood host
- add SSE heartbeat comments from server `:hb\n\n` every 10s to keep conn alive and detect proxied buffering
- use resume token logic: on reconnect include last event id so server can dedupe (if you can integrate)

eli-netops: additional network-side work: set MSS clamp on the proxy to 1400 or enable PMTU discovery path MTU fix; disable HTTP/1.0 translation and TLS response buffering; ensure `Connection: keep-alive` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` are passthrough.

june-acme: appreciate the list. Can Redwood suggest a server-side quick toggle we can flip on our Dedicated instance? Something to force heartbeat or chunk sizes?

matt-eng-runtime: yes — we can enable a temporary SSE heartbeat/flush mode on your Dedicated pool that inserts `:hb` comments every 8 seconds and forces a flush at 1KB boundaries (so proxies see frequent frames). That should reduce likelihood of mid-chunk truncation and make proxies less likely to buffer. It won't fix a hard RST/reassembly bug but helps.

travis-psm: I'll coordinate an off-hours window for the toggle and notify billing to avoid duplicate charge disputes while we triage. @sophia-support please confirm POA. :white_check_mark:

sophia-support: on it. @june-acme can you run this short test after toggle: 1) start streaming, 2) intentionally trigger proxy inspect (we can add a test header) to simulate, 3) capture whether stream contains `:hb` lines and whether reconnect duplicates tokens. Post results here.

deploy-bot: scheduled change for dedicated-pool acme-customer at 2023-11-01T02:00:00Z by matt-eng-runtime — change: enable-sse-heartbeat-flush (temporary).

june-acme: thanks all — testing now. First quick note: when we sent `Accept: text/event-stream` but proxy downgraded to `application/octet-stream` we got immediate close. I'll validate after toggle and post tcpdump + billing IDs.

matt-eng-runtime: thanks. long-term: we'll surface a Dedicated config option in Console: `streaming.proxy-friendly-mode` that enforces small flush windows and explicit SSE comment heartbeats; and we'll add resume/dedupe semantics tied to session ids to avoid double-billing on reconnect.

eli-netops: FYI if you need packet captures we can provide a pcap analyzer script that flags fragmented SSE payloads and reassembly failures. happy to share.

june-acme: test after toggle shows stream contains repeated `:hb` lines and client no longer sees mid-payload truncation in 10 runs. Billing team put a temporary hold on suspected duplicate invoices. Will follow up with final pcap. :thumbsup:

sophia-support: great progress — leaving this thread open until pcap + billing cleared. Thanks everyone.
